correctness.rationale: The exact two-colour wild-number/component identity reduces the claim to components of a hypergeometric G(n,m) and its complement. A fixed monochromatic cut has probability at most e 2^{-k(n-k)}. Counting all possible small nontrivial components proves the O(n^2 4^{-n}) error. The exact singleton expectation is n[(m)_{n-1}+(N-m)_{n-1}]/(N)_{n-1}; two singleton occurrences are exponentially smaller and cannot have opposite colours. The logarithmic expansion gives e^{-1} per colour. Exact independent exhaustive n=4..7 enumerations (359423 edge sets) and isolated-vertex rational identities pass, without substituting finite tests for the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The original random-equitable problem gave a vanishing limit but no scale. This supplies a sharp universal probability rate, an exact finite-population singleton approximation with exponentially small error, and a structural classification of rare failures. The e^{-1} conditioning factor distinguishes equal-sized color classes from independent colour flips; typical repair costs (one versus two or more wild edges) matter directly to spanning-network reliability.
